title: Capacity domains, reservations and workspace
summary: Workspace capacity is accounted against the real underlying capacity domain, not against pathnames. Reservations claim space before work starts and safety floors protect the host from consuming every free byte.
invariants: Several paths on the same filesystem share one capacity domain and must not have their free bytes added together.
Separate nodes/devices/filesystems remain separate capacity domains unless an explicit storage layer combines them.
Two 30 GiB nodes are two 30 GiB candidates, not one 60 GiB workspace for an ordinary non-distributed job.
Workspace allocation is a reservation/claim, not merely a contemporaneous df observation.
A pool can advertise WORKSPACE, DURABLE or BOTH physical roles while lifecycle safety separately determines whether it counts as durable.

provenance.claim: Regression proves shared-filesystem capacity-domain deduplication and reservation accounting.
